procedure: single-incision thoracoscopic (VATS) right upper lobectomy with systematic mediastinal lymph node dissection
phase: mediastinal lymph node dissection after the lobectomy; the station shown in this shot is not stated - most likely the upper mediastinal (right paratracheal) en bloc dissection (low confidence; alternatives: subcarinal or hilar)
sources: video 2 legend (Commons description = Additional file 2 legend of Jeon et al., J Cardiothorac Surg 2014, 9:66)
article full text PMC4022387: Surgical technique, Discussion, Figure 1-2 legends
notes: Station inference: the legend lists lower mediastinal, subcarinal, hilar and upper mediastinal nodes in that order, and the article describes them in the same order; data prep found cuts at 10.9, 12.1, 13.2 and 31.3 s, so 31.3-62.1 s is the last and longest shot, which fits the last-listed and most extensive step (upper mediastinal en bloc resection). This ordering argument is weak; organs specific to one station have expected_visibility 'unknown'. The cut at 31.3 s means 31.0-31.3 s belongs to the previous shot. Lobectomy instruments (endostapler, right-angle clamp with silastic drain) belong to video 1 and are not expected here. Extra keys: instruments[].id, organs[].sam_prompt_alt, background[].source.

patient.condition: right upper lobe adenocarcinoma (CT: 1.8 cm spiculated nodule, clinical T1aN0M0; pathology 2.4 x 1.4 cm, T1bN0M0, 38 nodes, all negative); right upper lobe already removed in this operation; coronary stent, diabetes, hypertension

organs.name: mediastinal lymph nodes and fat
organs.pathology: none (nodes negative on pathology); removed for staging
organs.expected_motion: grasped, lifted and pulled away from its bed; progressively detached by ultrasonic dissection and removed en bloc (large deformation, then separation from the scene)
organs.notes: Upper mediastinal hypothesis: fat block with nodes bounded by the RUL bronchus stump, subclavian artery, SVC and trachea. Subcarinal hypothesis: nodes between right and left main bronchi near the esophagus.

organs.name: mediastinal pleura
organs.expected_motion: incised; cut edges retract and move with the fat underneath
organs.notes: Article: pleura incised above the azygos vein for the upper mediastinal step. Transparent membrane: its video depth is the depth of what lies behind it.

organs.name: azygos vein
organs.expected_motion: elevated (lifted) by an instrument to open the paratracheal space (upper mediastinal step); otherwise static with transmitted cardiac pulsation
organs.notes: Named in all candidate stations (subcarinal Figure 1b, hilar nodes below it, upper mediastinal step lifts it), hence 'partial'.

organs.name: superior vena cava
organs.notes: Boundary of the upper mediastinal block (article, Figure 2a).

organs.name: trachea
organs.notes: Boundary of the upper mediastinal block (article, Figure 2a). Cartilage-ringed, stiff.

organs.name: right upper lobe bronchus stump
organs.pathology: divided and closed with an endostapler during the lobectomy
organs.expected_motion: static; may be pushed anteriorly by an instrument or the suction tip (described for the subcarinal step)
organs.notes: Lower boundary of the upper mediastinal block (Figure 2a); retracted for subcarinal access.

organs.name: right subclavian artery
organs.notes: Upper boundary of the upper mediastinal block (article).

organs.name: right lung (middle and lower lobes)
organs.pathology: deflated (one-lung ventilation of the left lung); upper lobe removed; inferior pulmonary ligament divided
organs.expected_motion: collapsed and passive; may be pushed out of the field; no ventilation motion
organs.notes: Hangs from the hilum only (inferior pulmonary ligament divided earlier).

organs.name: right main bronchus
organs.notes: Only if the shot is the subcarinal station (Figure 1b boundary).

organs.name: esophagus
organs.notes: Only if the shot is the subcarinal station (Figure 1b).

Article: nodes grasped with an endo-instrument through the posterior part of the incision; endo-graspers listed. 5 mm default (not stated).
Article: the suction tip was one option for pushing the divided bronchus forward (subcarinal step). Use in this shot not stated.

Stapled closed in video 1; not reopened.

camera.notes: Article. Inserted through the single 4 cm incision (5th intercostal space, anterior axillary line) with a wound protector; every instrument shares this incision, so shafts enter close together and nearly parallel to the scope (authors note instruments impinging on each other). Scope placed in the anterior part of the incision for the lower mediastinal step and in the centre for the subcarinal step; not stated for the upper mediastinal step. Patient in left lateral decubitus (right side up): gravity points from the right chest wall toward the mediastinum; the image orientation of gravity is unknown. Picture rows 60-417 (data prep).
